name: cc1101-tool
one_line: Arduino Pro Micro + CC1101 board driven from a plain USB serial terminal, for sub-GHz jamming and raw replay; no specialised host software.
why_notable: 481 stars, last commit 2025-12-23. Self-described cheap alternative to the YARD Stick One.

name: Flipper Zero SubGHz Module
one_line: CC1101-based sub-GHz radio module that connects to a Flipper Zero's SPI pins and externalizes sub-GHz capability so external antennas/amplifiers can be attached; requires JCMK's separate SPI Adapter Board.
why_notable: A standalone sub-GHz radio peripheral for Flipper Zero (CC1101), not currently represented among the DB's Flipper accessory entries; extends range/antenna flexibility beyond the Flipper's internal sub-GHz radio.
mcu: n/a (radio module, no MCU; TI CC1101)
has_battery: no, powered via Flipper Zero SPI header
has_ext_antenna: yes, antenna included, connects external antennas/amplifiers

name: Open Source Meshtastic Nibble
one_line: Open-source RFM95 LoRa (868/915MHz) mesh-networking node built around an RP2040 or ESP32-S3, sold as bare PCB, unsoldered kit, or fully soldered; runs Meshtastic firmware for encrypted off-grid mesh comms.
why_notable: Fully open-source (github.com/retiallc/nibble), debuted at 38C3 alongside a 'Hacker's Guide to Meshtastic' talk; flagged borderline because its core function is encrypted mesh networking/comms rather than an offensive or defensive security-testing primitive, though it's squarely hacker-con hardware.

name: Diabolic Parasite
one_line: Inline USB implant: the target's keyboard or mouse plugs into the Parasite's female port and the Parasite into the freed host port. Clones the passthrough device's hardware identity, logs keystrokes to a web UI, and wirelessly triggers injection with randomized typing cadence and ALT+Numpad layout bypass.
why_notable: Passive keylogging, identity cloning and remote injection in one covert implant.

name: Diabolic Drive
one_line: USB flash-drive-shaped device behaving as normal 64GB storage until wirelessly commanded over Wi-Fi to expose a HID keyboard interface and inject a stored payload; spoofs VID/PID/serial for both the storage and HID personas.
why_notable: Combines real flash storage, remote-triggered HID injection and hardware-ID spoofing in one drive.

name: USB Nugget (ESP32S2)
one_line: ESP32-S2 board with native USB, OLED screen and buttons that enumerates as a USB flash drive and HID keyboard for drag-and-drop keystroke-injection (BadUSB) payloads, remotely controllable over Wi-Fi.
why_notable: Open-source BadUSB platform with its own 'Nugget OS' firmware and CircuitPython payload repos (RetiaLLC/RubberNugget-CircuitPython, RetiaLLC/S2-Nugget on GitHub) — functionally a Wi-Fi-controlled, mass-storage-loadable alternative to the USB Rubber Ducky already in the DB.

name: MalDuino W
one_line: WiFi-controlled BadUSB device: run/edit/delete/download keystroke-injection scripts over a web interface instead of reprogramming via cable. Converted from GBP 49 at ~1.354 USD/GBP.
why_notable: Wireless variant of the MalDuino line letting an operator trigger payloads remotely over WiFi rather than needing physical reprogramming access.

name: MalDuino 3
one_line: Arduino-based BadUSB keystroke injector with 128MB onboard storage for file exfiltration, dual USB-A/C, and 34 keyboard-locale support. Converted from GBP 35 at ~1.354 USD/GBP.
why_notable: Current-generation MalDuino model with built-in exfiltration storage; distinct hardware revision from the MalDuino Elite already tracked.

name: O.MG Cable Programmer (USB A+C)
one_line: Programming/flashing tool for configuring O.MG Cable devices.
why_notable: Support tool for the already-tracked O.MG Cable line; included for completeness though it is an accessory rather than an attack device itself.

name: UsbSafe2
one_line: Inline USB dongle with a physical button to disable the data lines (anti-juice-jacking) and clamp output voltage/current at five selectable thresholds to protect the downstream device from a malicious or faulty host.
why_notable: Data blocker plus overvoltage/overcurrent cutoff; same niche as the tracked O.MG UnBlocker but a distinct older product.

name: USB Snake Box
one_line: CircuitPython microcontroller in a 3D-printed box with four buttons, each mapped to a different pre-programmed keystroke-injection payload.
why_notable: Multi-button physical BadUSB, a distinct form factor from tracked single-payload devices.

name: HackyPi
one_line: RP2040 USB stick with a 1.14in TFT and SD slot that emulates HID keyboard input and runs drag-and-drop cross-platform payload scripts.
why_notable: BadUSB board with an onboard display - not one of the tracked Digispark/CH552/pico-ducky designs.

name: BLE BadUSB (JDY-08)
one_line: ATmega32U4 + JDY-08 BLE module USB stick emulating keyboard and mouse and accepting remote command injection over BLE 4.0; open source, Arduino-programmable.
why_notable: BLE-remote-triggered BadUSB - a different attack surface from the Wi-Fi and onboard-payload devices tracked.

name: Wifi BadUSB
one_line: ATmega32U4 + ESP-12F USB stick acting as a HID injector and hosting its own Wi-Fi access point for control and reflashing; runs supremeDuck, wifi_ducky or ESPloitV2.
why_notable: Wi-Fi-controlled BadUSB from the same maker, distinct hardware from the BLE variants.

name: Programmable BadUSB Payload Cable USB-A to USB-C
one_line: USB-A to USB-C cable with an embedded microcontroller emulating HID and mass storage, storing multiple reprogrammable payloads, with an LED status indicator.
why_notable: Cable-form payload injector at a tenth the price of an O.MG Cable - worth comparing directly against it.

name: Mouse Jiggler
one_line: USB device that enumerates as a mouse and injects small, periodic cursor movements to prevent screen lock and away/idle status.
why_notable: Not an attack tool itself; a covert USB HID device commonly used operationally during physical or remote engagements to prevent session lockout.
